svg.text: W2 · K1 relay outputs → stack lights, buzzer, S1 lamp
Relay commons are jumpered to +12 V (fused F2). Relays switch +12 V out on NO. Tower common returns to 0 V.
Terminal order on the real board: VERIFY (pluggable 3-pin per CH,
silkscreen NO / C / NC). Relay LEDs mirror coil state.
Panel wiring K1→TB2: 18 AWG, color as shown.
Cable W-HL1: tower lead or 18/5 SJOOW to G5
Cable W-HL2: tower lead or 18/5 SJOOW to G6
Lead too short → splice in IP67 JB at mast, keep colors
TB1-13 0 V (W1) · in cable W-CS (6-cond), see W3
Lamp truth: firmware sets exactly ONE of CH1/CH2/CH3. CH4 = buzzer, CH5 = S1 lamp.
HL1 + HL2 in parallel at TB2 (one wire in, two out per level). 4-level terminals,
or 2 stacked 2-level terminals with a bridge. Each tower ≈ 3 W → F2 2 A is plenty.
Tower common polarity: meter it. If the common must be +12 V (common-anode tower):
move 205 to TB1 0 V and 306 to TB1 +12 V. Nothing else changes.
Typical lead colors: RD red · YE amber · GN green · WH or BN buzzer · BK common.
Relay NC contacts unused: leave empty. Don't wire anything to NC on CH1-CH3.
RFID PANEL BOX · RPB-001 · WIRING DIAGRAM
Gielow Pickles · G5 Croswell · one box per dock door
CH1-CH4 → TB2 → HL1 + HL2 stack lights · CH5 → S1 lamp · CH6-8 spare
Units: inches, AWG. Wire numbers are per potential: the same number on both ends and every jumper of one net. Ref RPB-001 rev 8 drawing + illustrated schematic.
